doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Count Basie, Artie Shaw and the soprano experiments
title: Dates with Basie and the unrecorded charts
summary: They fix Mandel's Basie stay as June to November 1953; his chart Straight Life was recorded and he laments how little of his work was.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So, you went with him in, as I understand it June of ‘53?
No, no, ‘52… well, I guess something like that, June… no, I went there sooner didn’t I?
It depends on how accurate Leonard Feather is. According to the notes I have it was June to November ‘53.
I guess it was, um-hm it was, we came to California and I stayed like I had planned to do originally.
So, you wrote at least one thing that got recorded right? A thing called, “Straight Life.”
Yeah, and I wrote some other stuff that didn’t…

I got something that was recorded from – I’ve had very bad track record of getting things recorded by bands, I’ve also had a terrible record of getting soundtracks for all the movies I’ve done, recorded. I have very little recorded history laying around, why, I don't know maybe that's my karma.
It never particularly bothered me, I was glad for the recordings I did get. Some guys just can't do anything without getting recorded.
And it comes back to haunt them, in some cases.
Yeah, I suppose, I don’t know.
